note: Health indicators AstroLife can actually collect, and the NASA catalog risks each one relates to. An indicator is collected because a risk it relates to belongs to a hazard of the mission. Relating an indicator to a risk never means the indicator can diagnose or rule out that risk.

indicators.label: Heart rate
indicators.why: NASA's cardiovascular adaptation risk concerns how circulation changes in altered gravity; a resting pulse is a basic observation the crew can log.

indicators.label: Estimated blood oxygen (SpO2)
indicators.why: NASA's hypoxia risk concerns reduced oxygen availability in closed, reduced-pressure environments; SpO2 is the related observation a fingertip sensor can estimate.

indicators.label: Sleep duration
indicators.why: NASA's sleep loss and circadian risk is tracked through reported sleep.

indicators.label: Prescribed exercise session
indicators.why: Exercise is NASA's main countermeasure for muscle, fitness and bone changes in altered gravity.
